QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_49

question.text: The Core Settlement Guarantee Fund (Core SGF) is maintained by:

answer.text: The clearing corporation, to guarantee settlement for each segment when a clearing member fails to honour commitments
Individual trading members for their own default protection
SEBI directly as a regulatory reserve
Client investors through a percentage of their trades

explanation.text: The Logic: Clearing corporations are required to have a Core Settlement Guarantee Fund to guarantee settlement for each segment and to fund obligations when a clearing member fails to honour commitments. The Trap: The Core SGF is held at the clearing corporation level for segment-wise settlement guarantee; it is not a trading member's own default reserve, a SEBI-held regulatory reserve, or a client-funded percentage levy. Note: Page 171 supports the Core SGF requirement and segment-wise settlement-guarantee role; the specific funding composition (clearing corporation, exchanges, and clearing members) is not stated in pages 171, 151, or 181 checked.
